statement: Construct a problem specification.
guidance: • The specification of a problem may include a problem statement, constraints and limitations, objectives and goals, input specifications, output specifications, evaluation criteria.
scope_qualifications: The specification of a problem may include a problem statement, constraints and limitations, objectives and goals, input specifications, output specifications, evaluation criteria.
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct a problem specification with relevant problem definition, constraints, inputs, outputs and evaluation criteria.
allowed_context: Problem specifications; named specification elements are may-include examples.

statement: Describe the fundamental concepts of computational thinking.
guidance: • Abstraction, algorithmic design, decomposition, pattern recognition
assessable_knowledge_skills: Describe abstraction, algorithmic design, decomposition and pattern recognition.
allowed_context: Computational problem-solving using the four listed concepts.

statement: Explain how applying computational thinking to fundamental concepts is used to approach and solve problems in computer science.
guidance:
• Computational thinking does not necessarily involve programming—it is a toolkit of available techniques for problem-solving.
• Real-world examples may include software development, data analysis, machine learning, database design, network security.
scope_qualifications: Real-world examples may include software development, data analysis, machine learning, database design, network security.
assessable_knowledge_skills: Explain application of computational thinking to approach and solve problems; programming is not required.
allowed_context: Real-world problems; software development, data analysis, ML, database design and network security are may-include examples.

statement: Trace flowcharts for a range of programming algorithms.
guidance:
• Use of standard flowchart symbols to depict processes, decisions and flows of control
• Standard flowchart symbols: Connector, Decision, Flowline, Input/Output, Process/Operation, Start/End
• Flowcharts for execution flow, to track changes in variables and to determine output
assessable_knowledge_skills: Trace standard-symbol flowcharts, track variables and determine outputs.
allowed_context: A range of programming-algorithm flowcharts using listed standard symbols.

statement: Construct and trace programs using a range of global and local variables of various data types.
guidance: • Data types: Boolean value, char, decimal, integer, string
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct and trace programs using global/local variables and the listed data types.
allowed_context: Python programs and relevant inputs/failures/debugging scenarios within the stated scope.

statement: Construct programs that can extract and manipulate substrings.
guidance: • Writing of programs that accurately identify and extract substrings from given strings, demonstrating the ability to perform various manipulations, such as altering, concatenating or replacing
scope_qualifications: Writing of programs that accurately identify and extract substrings from given strings, demonstrating the ability to perform various manipulations, such as altering, concatenating or replacing
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct programs that extract and manipulate substrings.
allowed_context: Python programs and relevant inputs/failures/debugging scenarios within the stated scope.

statement: Describe how programs use common exception handling techniques.
guidance:
• Potential points of failure in a program must include unexpected inputs, resource unavailability, logic errors.
• The role of exception handling in developing programs
• Exception handling constructs that effectively manage errors must include try/catch in Java, and try/except in Python, along with the finally block.
scope_qualifications: Potential points of failure in a program must include unexpected inputs, resource unavailability, logic errors. | Exception handling constructs that effectively manage errors must include try/catch in Java, and try/except in Python, along with the finally block.
assessable_knowledge_skills: Describe failure points, exception handling and try/except/finally in Python.
allowed_context: Python programs and relevant inputs/failures/debugging scenarios within the stated scope.

statement: Construct and use common debugging techniques.
guidance: • Debugging techniques may include trace tables, breakpoint debugging, print statements and step-by-step code execution.
scope_qualifications: Debugging techniques may include trace tables, breakpoint debugging, print statements and step-by-step code execution.
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct and use debugging techniques; named techniques are non-exhaustive examples.
allowed_context: Python programs and relevant inputs/failures/debugging scenarios within the stated scope.

statement: Compare static and dynamic data structures.
guidance:
• The fundamental differences between static and dynamic data structures, including their underlying mechanisms for memory allocation and resizing
• The advantages and disadvantages of each type in various scenarios, considering factors such as speed, memory usage, flexibility
scope_qualifications: The advantages and disadvantages of each type in various scenarios, considering factors such as speed, memory usage, flexibility
assessable_knowledge_skills: Compare static/dynamic structures in allocation, resizing, speed, memory usage and flexibility.
allowed_context: Data-structure choices and Python List programs, stack/queue problems with performance and memory considerations.

statement: Construct programs that apply arrays and Lists.
guidance:
• One-dimensional (1D) arrays, two-dimensional (2D) arrays, ArrayLists in Java
• One-dimensional (1D) Lists and two-dimensional (2D) Lists in Python
• Add, remove and traverse elements in a dynamic list
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct programs using 1D/2D Python Lists, adding, removing and traversing dynamic-list elements.
allowed_context: Data-structure choices and Python List programs, stack/queue problems with performance and memory considerations.

statement: Explain the concept of a stack as a “last in, first out” (LIFO) data structure.
guidance:
• Must include fundamental operations such as push, pop, peek and isEmpty
• How stack operations impact both performance and memory usage
• An appropriate stack for a specific problem
scope_qualifications: Must include fundamental operations such as push, pop, peek and isEmpty
assessable_knowledge_skills: Explain LIFO stacks, named operations, performance/memory impact and appropriate selection.
allowed_context: Data-structure choices and Python List programs, stack/queue problems with performance and memory considerations.

statement: Explain the concept of a queue as a “first in, first out” (FIFO) data structure.
guidance:
• Must include fundamental operations such as enqueue, dequeue, front and isEmpty
• How queue operations impact both performance and memory usage
• An appropriate queue for a specific problem
scope_qualifications: Must include fundamental operations such as enqueue, dequeue, front and isEmpty
assessable_knowledge_skills: Explain FIFO queues, named operations, performance/memory impact and appropriate selection.
allowed_context: Data-structure choices and Python List programs, stack/queue problems with performance and memory considerations.

statement: Construct programs that implement the correct sequence of code instructions to meet program objectives.
guidance:
• The impact of instruction order on program functionality
• Ways to avoid errors, such as infinite loops, deadlock, incorrect output
scope_qualifications: Ways to avoid errors, such as infinite loops, deadlock, incorrect output
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct correctly sequenced programs and avoid instruction-order errors.
allowed_context: Python programs selected to meet specified objectives, using the relevant constructs and functions.

statement: Construct programs utilizing appropriate selection structures.
guidance:
• Must include: if, else, else if (Java), elif (Python), to execute different code blocks based on specified conditions
• Selection structures with or without Boolean operators (AND, OR, NOT) and/or relational operators (<, <=, >, >=, ==, !=) to control program flow effectively
scope_qualifications: Must include: if, else, else if (Java), elif (Python), to execute different code blocks based on specified conditions
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct selection with Python if/else/elif, Boolean and relational operators.
allowed_context: Python programs selected to meet specified objectives, using the relevant constructs and functions.

statement: Construct programs that utilize looping structures to perform repeated actions.
guidance:
• Types of loops, including counted loops and conditional loops, and appropriate use of each type
• Conditional statements within loops, using Boolean and/or relational operators to govern the loop’s execution
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct counted/conditional loops and conditions governing execution.
allowed_context: Python programs selected to meet specified objectives, using the relevant constructs and functions.

statement: Construct functions and modularization.
guidance:
• Functions to define reusable blocks of code with different inputs
• Modularization to create well-structured, reusable and maintainable code
• The principles of scope (local versus global)
• The benefits of code modularization, applying this concept to various programming scenarios
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct reusable functions and modular programs; apply local/global scope.
allowed_context: Python programs selected to meet specified objectives, using the relevant constructs and functions.

statement: Describe the efficiency of specific algorithms by calculating their Big O notation to analyse their scalability.
guidance:
• The time and space complexities of algorithms and calculating Big O notation
• Algorithm choice based on scalability and efficiency requirements
assessable_knowledge_skills: Calculate time/space Big O and describe scalability and efficiency in algorithm choice.
allowed_context: Specific algorithms with assessable time/space scalability and efficiency requirements.

statement: Construct and trace algorithms to implement a linear search and a binary search for data retrieval.
guidance:
• The differences in efficiency between different methods of linear and binary search
• Use of search technique based on efficiency requirements—for example, searching a database for a sorted/indexed list of names to find a phone number, versus searching by the number to identify the name
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct and trace linear/binary searches; compare efficiency and select an appropriate technique.
allowed_context: Linear/binary search and efficiency-driven technique selection; the sorted/indexed names/phone-number example illustrates context.

statement: Construct and trace algorithms to implement bubble sort and selection sort, evaluating their time and space complexities.
guidance:
• The time and space complexities of each algorithm, denoted by their respective Big O notations
• The advantages and disadvantages of each algorithm in terms of efficiency across various data sets
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct and trace bubble/selection sort and evaluate time/space complexity and relative efficiency.
allowed_context: Bubble/selection sort across various data sets.

statement: Explain the fundamental concept of recursion and its applications in programming. (HL only)
guidance:
• The fundamentals of recursion and its advantages and limitations
• The utility of recursion in solving problems that can be broken down into smaller, similar sub-problems
• Recursive algorithms, including but not limited to quicksort
• The limitations of recursion, including complexity and memory usage
• Situations that best suit the use of recursion, including fractal image creation, traversing binary trees, sorting algorithms
scope_qualifications: Recursive algorithms, including but not limited to quicksort
assessable_knowledge_skills: Explain recursion, advantages/limitations, applications and memory/complexity; conceptual recursive examples include quicksort.
allowed_context: Problems decomposable into smaller similar subproblems; quicksort, fractal image creation, binary-tree traversal and sorting are included conceptual contexts.

statement: Construct and trace recursive algorithms in a programming language. (HL only)
guidance: • Simple, non-branching recursive algorithms in programming only
scope_qualifications: Simple, non-branching recursive algorithms in programming only
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct and trace simple, non-branching recursive algorithms only.
allowed_context: Simple, non-branching recursive programs only; do not turn conceptual quicksort coverage into a requirement to construct branching recursion.

statement: Construct code to perform file-processing operations.
guidance:
• Programs that manipulate text files
• Opening a sequential file in various modes (read, write, append)
• How to read from and write to files, append data to an existing file, and close a file once operations are completed
• Classes for Java users may include Scanner, FileWriter, BufferedReader.
• Functions for Python users may include open(), read(), readline(), write(), close().
scope_qualifications: Classes for Java users may include Scanner, FileWriter, BufferedReader. | Functions for Python users may include open(), read(), readline(), write(), close().
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct sequential text-file code to open read/write/append, read, write, append and close.
allowed_context: Sequential text files and read/write/append modes. Listed Python functions are may-include examples.

subtopic: B3.1 Fundamentals of OOP for a single class
statement: Evaluate the fundamentals of OOP.
guidance:
• Model real-world entities using OOP concepts: classes, objects, inheritance, encapsulation, polymorphism
• The advantages and disadvantages of using OOP in various programming scenarios
assessable_knowledge_skills: Evaluate OOP concepts and advantages/disadvantages for modelling real-world entities.
allowed_context: OOP scenarios modelling entities, single-class design/code, UML and class/object state, as specified.

subtopic: B3.1 Fundamentals of OOP for a single class
statement: Construct a design of classes, their methods and behaviour.
guidance:
• Classes and their methods, based on application requirements
• The use of unified modelling language (UML) class diagrams to represent class relationships, attributes and methods, to aid effective software design and planning
assessable_knowledge_skills: Design classes, methods and behaviour; use UML class diagrams for relationships, attributes and methods.
allowed_context: OOP scenarios modelling entities, single-class design/code, UML and class/object state, as specified.

subtopic: B3.1 Fundamentals of OOP for a single class
statement: Distinguish between static and non-static variables and methods.
guidance:
• The differences between static and non-static variables and methods, including their usage and scope
• When to use instance variables instead of class variables, and how to apply these concepts effectively in code
assessable_knowledge_skills: Distinguish static/non-static variables/methods, usage/scope, instance/class variables and code application.
allowed_context: OOP scenarios modelling entities, single-class design/code, UML and class/object state, as specified.

subtopic: B3.1 Fundamentals of OOP for a single class
statement: Construct code to define classes and instantiate objects.
guidance:
• How to define classes and create objects from those classes
• The role of constructors in initializing an object's state, setting initial values for its attributes to define its condition or characteristics at the time of creation
assessable_knowledge_skills: Define classes, instantiate objects and initialize state through constructors.
allowed_context: OOP scenarios modelling entities, single-class design/code, UML and class/object state, as specified.

subtopic: B3.1 Fundamentals of OOP for a single class
statement: Explain and apply the concepts of encapsulation and information hiding in OOP.
guidance:
• The principles of encapsulation and information hiding
• Apply access modifiers such as private and public
• Controlling access to class members
• The importance of limiting access to maintain the integrity and security of an object's state
scope_qualifications: Apply access modifiers such as private and public
assessable_knowledge_skills: Explain/apply encapsulation, information hiding, access control and protection of object state.
allowed_context: OOP scenarios modelling entities, single-class design/code, UML and class/object state, as specified.

subtopic: B3.2 Fundamentals of OOP for multiple classes (HL only)
statement: Explain and apply the concept of inheritance in OOP to promote code reusability.
guidance:
• How inheritance enables a hierarchical relationship between parent and child classes
• Extending existing classes, utilizing inheritance to reuse and extend functionalities
• The impact of inheritance on access to parent class members with different access modifiers (private, public, protected, default)
assessable_knowledge_skills: Explain/apply inheritance, reuse/extensions and the effect of parent-member access restrictions.
allowed_context: Multiple-class OOP scenarios using the specified inheritance/polymorphism/abstraction/relationships/design-pattern scope.

subtopic: B3.2 Fundamentals of OOP for multiple classes (HL only)
statement: Construct code to model polymorphism and its various forms, such as method overriding.
guidance:
• The principle of polymorphism and how it contributes to code flexibility and reusability
• How to implement dynamic polymorphic behaviour through mechanisms like method overriding
• How to apply static polymorphic behaviour to maximize code efficiency
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct polymorphic code, method overriding and dynamic/static polymorphic behaviour within language-appropriate semantics.
allowed_context: Multiple-class OOP scenarios using the specified inheritance/polymorphism/abstraction/relationships/design-pattern scope.

subtopic: B3.2 Fundamentals of OOP for multiple classes (HL only)
statement: Explain the concept of abstraction in OOP.
guidance:
• The significance of abstraction in the development of modular code fragments
• The use of abstract classes to establish common interfaces for sub-classes
assessable_knowledge_skills: Explain abstraction, modular code and abstract classes providing common subclass interfaces.
allowed_context: Multiple-class OOP scenarios using the specified inheritance/polymorphism/abstraction/relationships/design-pattern scope.

subtopic: B3.2 Fundamentals of OOP for multiple classes (HL only)
statement: Explain the role of composition and aggregation in class relationships.
guidance:
• How to design objects by leveraging smaller component objects through composition and aggregation
• That aggregation implies that the subcomponents can function independently of the aggregating class, while in composition, the subcomponents are tightly coupled and cannot exist outside the aggregating class
assessable_knowledge_skills: Explain composition/aggregation, design with components and distinguish dependent versus independent component lifetimes.
allowed_context: Multiple-class OOP scenarios using the specified inheritance/polymorphism/abstraction/relationships/design-pattern scope.

subtopic: B3.2 Fundamentals of OOP for multiple classes (HL only)
statement: Explain commonly used design patterns in OOP.
guidance:
• The key design patterns such as singleton, factory and observer
• The application of design patterns in solving recurring programming challenges
scope_qualifications: The key design patterns such as singleton, factory and observer
assessable_knowledge_skills: Explain common OOP design patterns and recurring-problem applications; named patterns include singleton, factory and observer.
allowed_context: Multiple-class OOP scenarios using the specified inheritance/polymorphism/abstraction/relationships/design-pattern scope.

statement: Explain the properties and purpose of ADTs in programming.
guidance: • The core principles of ADTs, including their purpose in providing a high-level description of data structures and their associated operations
assessable_knowledge_skills: Explain ADT properties/purpose as high-level structures and associated operations.
allowed_context: Specified ADTs and operations, diagrammatic linked lists/BSTs, Python implementations where requested, memory/performance comparisons.

statement: Evaluate linked lists.
guidance:
• Lists must include singly, doubly, circular
• Sketch of linked lists and implementation of basic operations diagrammatically, such as insertion, deletion, traversal, search
• The advantages and disadvantages of using linked lists over other data structures like arrays, particularly in terms of memory utilization and performance
scope_qualifications: Lists must include singly, doubly, circular | Sketch of linked lists and implementation of basic operations diagrammatically, such as insertion, deletion, traversal, search
assessable_knowledge_skills: Evaluate singly/doubly/circular linked lists, sketch operations and compare memory/performance with arrays.
allowed_context: Specified ADTs and operations, diagrammatic linked lists/BSTs, Python implementations where requested, memory/performance comparisons.

statement: Construct and apply linked lists: singly, doubly and circular.
guidance: • The basic operations on a linked list, such as insertion, deletion, traversal, search
scope_qualifications: The basic operations on a linked list, such as insertion, deletion, traversal, search
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct/apply singly/doubly/circular linked lists and basic operations.
allowed_context: Specified ADTs and operations, diagrammatic linked lists/BSTs, Python implementations where requested, memory/performance comparisons.

statement: Explain the structures and properties of BSTs.
guidance:
• How binary search trees (BSTs) are used for data organization
• Insert, delete, traverse and searching nodes in a BST
• Sketching a BST as a tree diagram
assessable_knowledge_skills: Explain BST structures/properties and organization; insert/delete/traverse/search nodes and sketch BSTs.
allowed_context: Specified ADTs and operations, diagrammatic linked lists/BSTs, Python implementations where requested, memory/performance comparisons.

statement: Construct and apply sets as an ADT.
guidance:
• The fundamental characteristics of sets, including their unordered nature and the uniqueness of elements
• Operations: union, intersection and difference
• Code to check if an element is in a set, to add an element to a set, to remove an element, and to check whether one set is a subset/superset of another set
assessable_knowledge_skills: Construct/apply unordered unique-element sets, union/intersection/difference, membership/add/remove and subset/superset code.
allowed_context: Specified ADTs and operations, diagrammatic linked lists/BSTs, Python implementations where requested, memory/performance comparisons.

statement: Explain the core principles of ADTs.
guidance:
• High-level description of data structures and their associated operations and purpose
• The underlying mechanics of hash tables, including hashing functions, collision resolution strategies and load factors
• The underlying mechanics of sets to store and manage data
• HashMap and HashSet in Java; dict and set in Python
assessable_knowledge_skills: Explain ADT principles, hash mechanics/functions/collisions/load factors, set mechanics and Python dict/set.
allowed_context: Specified ADTs and operations, diagrammatic linked lists/BSTs, Python implementations where requested, memory/performance comparisons.
